chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:
The maternal uncle and the maternal aunt inherit when there is no one else with them.
Indeed, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, says: 'And those of kinship are nearer to one another in the Book of Allah.'
ai.seo_question: Who inherits if there are no parents, children, or spouse?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi establishes the inheritance rights of the maternal uncle and aunt, grounding their claim in the Quranic principle of 'ulu al-arham' (those of kinship). In Shia jurisprudence, this serves as a primary textual basis for the concept of 'dhawu al-arham' (relatives by blood not explicitly mentioned in fixed shares), particularly when no closer agnatic or cognatic heirs exist. The narration highlights the theological emphasis on blood ties as a divine criterion for inheritance distribution.
